items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: In fact we’re going to do it tonight, the Breezin’ Along group. I’ll have fun with that. Because Howard Alden can read my mind, Bucky plays nonparalleled rhythm, nobody plays better than him.

ctx.x: That’s something to sustain a band like that too without a bass player I think.

Oh we were brilliant. We really enjoyed. I made a conscious effort to play trios. So I did a trio with Art Hodes and Don DeMicheal, and then they died. And then it was Ralph Sutton and Gus Johnson and Gus Johnson died. Then I did one with Dick Wellstood and Bobby Rosengarden, and Dick died. And then, you know, but after a while, so like I switched to guitars. And they’re all alive. In fact we’re going to do it tonight, the Breezin’ Along group. I’ll have fun with that. Because Howard Alden can read my mind, Bucky…

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

ctx.x: Well, it’s going to be great. It’s going to be great. You’re in good company with some of the other folks I’ve seen, and it’s nice to have you back here. You’ve been here a number of times.
Yes. With Kenny Davern and company.

Yes. And we have some fireworks going on in the background, because everybody’s celebrating. I kind of wish we had been taping during our dinner just before this, because you were saying some great stuff. I was fascinated by your description of your family life and being a young person during the Depression.
